content.text: I'll create a channel beam (C-beam) that is 70mm wide, 40mm high, 450mm long, with 5mm wall thickness, open on the top. Let me start by calculating the necessary dimensions for creating this shape using blocks.

input.PythonCode:
# Channel beam dimensions
width = 70  # mm
height = 40  # mm
length = 450  # mm
wall_thickness = 5  # mm

# For a C-beam open on top, we need:
# 1. Main block (full dimensions)
# 2. Subtract inner cavity

# Main block dimensions
main_x = length
main_y = width
main_z = height

# Inner cavity to subtract (creating the channel)
# The cavity starts at wall_thickness from bottom and sides
cavity_x = length  # Full length
cavity_y = width - 2 * wall_thickness  # Width minus two side walls
cavity_z = height - wall_thickness  # Height minus bottom wall

# Cavity position (offset from origin)
cavity_x_pos = 0  # Same start as main block
cavity_y_pos = wall_thickness  # Offset by wall thickness from left
cavity_z_pos = wall_thickness  # Offset by wall thickness from bottom

print(f"Main block dimensions: {main_x} x {main_y} x {main_z} mm")
print(f"Main block position: (0, 0, 0)")
print(f"Cavity dimensions: {cavity_x} x {cavity_y} x {cavity_z} mm")
print(f"Cavity position: ({cavity_x_pos}, {cavity_y_pos}, {cavity_z_pos})")
